ogTitle: Top 10 Popular Restaurants in Pattani 2026 — Eat Like a Local
ogDesc: A four-generation kai kho lae legend, the richly topped Khao Yam Racha, Laem Nok seaside seafood, and a café in a century-old tin factory — 10 Pattani spots locals actually bring their friends to.
eyebrow: Eat Like a Pattani Local · Updated 2026
intro: Pattani is a city where Malay, Chinese, and Thai cooking have shared the same table for centuries. Start the morning with charcoal-grilled kai kho lae drenched in coconut curry sauce, move on to a herb-packed khao yam at midday, then settle in for seafood by the sea at Laem Nok in the evening. We've gathered 10 restaurants that Pattani locals genuinely take their friends to — from a four-generation legend to a beautifully converted tin-factory café.

blocks.html:
If you had to explain Pattani's food scene to a friend, you'd start here. This old port city has long blended Malay, Hokkien Chinese, and Thai cultures, giving it a cuisine you'd struggle to find anywhere else. Strolling through the old town along the Pattani River you'll find pastel Sino-Portuguese shophouses with cafés tucked inside buildings a hundred years old. Drive out towards Rusamilae and Laem Nok and you'll hit seafood restaurants taking deliveries straight off local fishing boats. The city's signature dish is kai kho lae — chicken grilled over charcoal, dipped in coconut curry and grilled again up to three times — alongside khao yam, where a full basket of herbs meets a fish-paste dressing. It's a flavour that clings to southerners for life.

This list has the real deal: Kai Kho Lae Yi Yoh Ramgomutt, a four-generation family recipe with a coconut sauce simmered for three hours and no MSG; Kama Khao Yam Racha on Naklua Road, earned its royal-khao-yam reputation through sheer generosity of toppings; Sun Kum Pu (Sea the Sun), a popular halal seafood spot in Rusamilae where crab fried rice and crab noodle curry are non-negotiable orders; and Kruwa Madam Laem Nok, where you sit over the sea eating fat garlic prawns. The café crowd has Rong Peep, a converted tin factory turned retro dining room serving crispy rad na and lava-egg noodles. Read on restaurant by restaurant — one day in Pattani is enough to eat very well.

blocks.name: Kai Kho Lae Yi Yoh Ramgomutt
blocks.area: Ramgomutt Road Soi 4, Mueang Pattani District
blocks.signature: Charcoal-grilled kai kho lae (grilled chicken) with rich coconut curry sauce
blocks.descHtml:
When people talk about food you must try in Pattani, Kai Kho Lae Yi Yoh Ramgomutt is one of the first names mentioned. This small shop in Soi 4 on Ramgomutt Road is the province's original kai kho lae. The recipe started in Grandma Mawtae's kitchen and has been passed down through four generations — a great starting meal for anyone wanting genuine Deep South flavours from the moment they arrive.

The star is chicken grilled over charcoal and basted with a rich coconut curry sauce. The technique is the secret: the chicken is grilled until fragrant, then dipped in the sauce and grilled again — three rounds in total, around 10–15 minutes per skewer. The meat soaks up the sauce and delivers a sweet-creamy richness cut with a light sourness from tamarind. The sauce is simmered from coconut milk, dried chillies, sugar, garlic, shallots, salt, and ginger for hours. A point many fans love: no MSG — the flavour is all from the curry paste. The must-orders are kai kho lae legs, breasts, and wings; if you want something different, there's also pla kho lae (fish) and hoi kho lae (shellfish).

Prices are very reasonable: around 45–50 THB per piece; offal and smaller pieces start in the tens. Whether you come solo or with a group, the bill stays light. The stall is a simple charcoal grill roadside setup — clouds of charcoal smoke drift down the soi long before you arrive, a smell Pattani people know well. The food is halal, comfortable for Muslim visitors.

Worth knowing: the stall grills to order and popular cuts sell out fast. Come between mid-morning and early afternoon to ensure you get everything. During festivals or holidays expect a queue, but a flavour passed down four generations is worth the wait — and it keeps both locals and visitors coming back without fail.
blocks.bestFor: First meal in the province, tasting the original local dish
blocks.hours: Mid-morning to early afternoon — sells out fast
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative image: curry · Takeaway / Wikimedia (CC BY-SA 3.0)

blocks.name: Nasi Dakae Sabarang
blocks.signature: Nasi dakae — coconut-steamed rice with tuna coconut curry, boiled egg, and sama (spiced fish relish) — eaten alongside the khao yam stall next door
blocks.descHtml:
If you wake up in Pattani and want a genuinely local breakfast — the kind the neighbourhood actually eats — Nasi Dakae Sabarang is the first name people here will give you. This small shop behind Benchamarachutit School on Sabarang Road has been selling nasi dakae for over 30 years, becoming a breakfast memory for multiple generations. It's perfect for anyone wanting to try authentic Deep South flavours, or a traveller arriving in Pattani who wants to start the day with something you simply can't find elsewhere.

The star is nasi dakae — rice steamed with fragrant coconut cream, topped with rich braised tuna coconut curry, served with a boiled egg and sama (a sweet-spicy fish relish). Locals often order khao yam from the stall next door to eat alongside it, getting both the richness of coconut and the freshness of khao yam in one sitting. The tuna curry is rounded and creamy with a good hit of curry spice — moderately spiced, not overpowering, comfortable for children and adults alike. It's the kind of homey flavour that fills you without weighing you down.

Prices are very accessible — around 35 THB per plate, and a complete meal stays well under 100 THB. The atmosphere is a traditional breakfast-stall setup: simple, unfussy, warm in the way a neighbourhood regular is. The food is Muslim/halal. The key thing to know: the stall opens only in the morning, roughly 6 a.m. to 9 a.m., and food runs out fast. Come early if you want both nasi dakae and khao yam — arriving late risks missing out entirely.

This stall makes the popular list because it's both delicious and a genuine Pattani breakfast legend. Locals have been returning for decades, and it's almost always the first place Pattani residents take out-of-town friends. If you visit Pattani and leave without trying nasi dakae at Sabarang, you haven't really arrived.
mustOrder: Nasi dakae (coconut rice with tuna curry + boiled egg + sama)
Khao yam from the next-door stall — eat them together
blocks.bestFor: Authentic local breakfast — come early before it sells out
blocks.spice: Medium, fragrant curry spice, not overpowering

blocks.name: Sun Kum Pu Pattani Branch
blocks.area: Charoen Pradit Road Soi 5, Rusamilae Sub-district, Mueang Pattani District, Pattani Province
blocks.signature: Crab fried rice, crab roe, crab noodle curry, fresh prawn salad, fresh seafood — crab, prawn, shellfish, fish
blocks.descHtml:
If you're in Pattani and want a full crab feast without doing the shelling yourself, Sun Kum Pu is the place locals point to almost unanimously. This halal seafood restaurant in Charoen Pradit Road Soi 5 in the Rusamilae area has been open long enough to become a household name for crab lovers in this city. Every table seems to order Langkasuka crab fried rice — generous with the crab meat — alongside crab roe, which many visitors come back for specifically. Craving something spicy? There's fresh prawn salad, crab noodle curry, and a full selection of fresh crab, prawn, shellfish, and fish dishes.

The flavour profile leans boldly southern, and the food community consistently praises it: fresh ingredients, firm textures, reasonable prices for the quantity. Some reviewers rave about getting a pile of crab without having to pick the shells yourself; others single out the oysters as large and wonderfully fresh, sourced locally. The owner is warm and approachable, the atmosphere is relaxed, and it works equally well for a family meal or a group outing. One practical note: parking is limited, and you may need to park on the roadside — if you're coming as a larger group or during peak hours, allow a little extra time.

Per-person spending runs roughly 100–200-odd THB: crab fried rice 179 THB, fresh prawn salad 169 THB, crab noodle curry set 60 THB. Good value for a restaurant where crab is the headline act. Open daily 11:00–21:00. Halal — Muslim guests are welcome without concern.
blocks.bestFor: Fresh seafood meal with family or a group of friends

blocks.name: Kama Khao Yam Racha
blocks.area: Naklua Road, Aneao Sub-district, Mueang Pattani District, Pattani Province
blocks.signature: Royal khao yam (herb rice salad) served with turmeric-salt-grilled fish (sea bass, mackerel, hardtail) and a full basket of herb garnishes
blocks.descHtml:
Ask anyone in Pattani where to get khao yam and you'll almost always hear one name: Kama Khao Yam Racha. This small local shop on Naklua Road in the Aneao sub-district of Pattani's old town has been around long enough to become the default answer. It's the place for anyone wanting genuine southern Thai flavours as locals eat them — not a version dialled down for tourists. Come alone, as a couple, or bring the whole family for a long late-afternoon lunch.

The star is the Racha khao yam, served with a basket overflowing with herb garnishes — long beans, wild betel leaves, lemongrass, and seasonal vegetables — alongside a budu fish sauce dressing that is the soul of the dish. Toss it together and you get sour, salty, sweet, and a gentle heat in one mouthful. What sets this place apart is the grilled fish: always order the turmeric-salt fish alongside — sea bass, mackerel, or hardtail — grilled until hissing with the scent of salt and turmeric, the sweetness of the flesh cutting perfectly against the khao yam. Reviewers consistently say the dish only reaches its peak with the grilled fish. Add grilled sataw beans and it's even better.

Beyond khao yam and grilled fish, the menu has other local dishes: tu pa su tong, coconut-milk prawn mi noodles, la sae, and desserts like coconut black sticky rice. Prices are very friendly — khao yam starts in the tens, and most people pay under 100 THB per head. The restaurant is halal, and reviewers call the owner warm and welcoming — the feel of eating at someone's house. On Wongnai the shop scores around 4.3 with comments like "exactly as delicious as it's always been."

Before you go: the shop opens afternoon to evening, roughly 15:00–22:00, Sunday to Friday (usually closed Saturday). It's next to the doctor's clinic on Naklua Road Soi 3 — easy to find in the city centre. There's parking and a prayer room. Some items, especially the grilled fish, sell out earlier in the evening — come before nightfall for the best selection.
blocks.bestFor: First meal in the province, experiencing authentic southern khao yam

blocks.name: Bungara Raya Restaurant (C.S. Pattani Hotel)
blocks.signature: Traditional Malay pulled tea, crispy roti, southern sour curry, salt-cured gurami fish, shrimp paste fried rice
blocks.descHtml:
If you want a comfortable, air-conditioned, well-served meal in Pattani where you can taste genuine southern flavours all in one sitting, Bungara Raya at the C.S. Pattani Hotel is the answer locals tend to recommend. The restaurant sits in an established hotel at the heart of the Rusamilae area and has been a go-to for family lunches and business entertaining for years. Everything is halal, and the menu ranges from Pattani local dishes to Thai, Chinese, and European options — suitable for solo diners, families, or groups.

Must-orders: the traditional Malay pulled tea (cha chak), stretched back and forth until the foam is soft, rich, and sweet — best with crispy roti or roti with green curry. For a rice meal, don't miss the southern sour curry with sea bass, which is rounded without being overpowering; the salt-cured gurami fish, fried until aromatic; and the shrimp-paste fried rice, a favourite repeat order. Fans of the restaurant's special dishes also praise the braised sea cucumber with red sauce, duck prepared C.S.-style, and soft-shell crab with garlic.

Reviews consistently praise quick service, generous portions, and excellent care — some mentioning live folk music on certain evenings. One honest note from reviewers: the sour curry isn't very spicy, which is actually a plus for those who can't take heat and for international guests. Several reviewers confirm the spices are complex but foreigners can handle them. Per-head price runs 101–250 THB — good value for a hotel restaurant.

Address: 99/9 Moo 4 Nong Chik Road, Rusamilae Sub-district, Mueang Pattani. Parking is easy from the hotel car park. Open daily 06:30–23:00, with a breakfast buffet 06:30–10:00. During Ramadan it gets packed — call ahead to book a table.
mustOrder: Crispy roti / roti with green curry
Southern sour curry with sea bass
blocks.bestFor: Family meal or business entertaining, air-conditioned comfort
blocks.spice: Mild–medium (sour curry is not heavily spiced)

blocks.name: Khao Man Kai Ko Chiu
blocks.signature: Smooth khao man kai (Hainanese chicken rice), signature dipping sauce, roast pork rice, braised pork rib soup with Chinese herbs
blocks.descHtml:
If you're in Pattani and want a breakfast that locals have been devoted to for decades, Khao Man Kai Ko Chiu is the first name out of their mouths. This small single-shophouse on Pattaniphirom Road in the old-town area — the riverside zone near the Pattani River, opposite the Pattani Yakult outlet — has been here for over 30 years. It's ideal for an early start before walking the old town.

The star is the home-style khao man kai: chicken that's pleasantly tender without falling apart, rice that separates cleanly without being greasy. Reviewers consistently praise the dipping sauce as the real highlight — a fermented soybean paste blended with garlic, chilli, and dark soy sauce, rounded and deep. Two other dishes that go with it constantly: roast pork rice, juicy-sweet and not dry; and the braised pork rib soup with Chinese herbs, fragrant throughout the bowl with rib meat that falls easily from the bone — a dish many say cannot be missed.

Atmosphere is simple shophouse fare: not many tables, fills up fast by mid-morning, quick service, friendly owner. Per-head spend stays under 100 THB — excellent value. Locals and reviewers consistently rank this among the best and cleanest khao man kai spots in the city. On Wongnai it scores around 4.1 stars, reflecting steady long-term popularity.

Worth knowing: the shop opens morning to early afternoon, 07:00–13:00, and often sells out before closing. If you intend to come, aim for early to mid-morning to be safe. Portions are a comfortable size — if you eat a lot, you can order extra rice. Parking in the old-town area is limited; allow a little time to find a space.
mustOrder: Braised pork rib soup with Chinese herbs
blocks.bestFor: Morning to midday meal before exploring the old town, budget-friendly
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative image: chicken rice · Pauloleong2002 / Wikimedia (CC BY-SA 4.0)

blocks.name: Kruwa Madam Laem Nok
blocks.area: Laem Nok Village, Moo 9, Bana Sub-district, Mueang Pattani District, Pattani Province
blocks.signature: Large garlic fried prawns, fresh seafood sourced from local fishing boats, sea views at Laem Nok
blocks.priceRange: 100–250 THB/dish (crab, prawn, shellfish by the kilo)
blocks.descHtml:
Kruwa Madam Laem Nok is a halal seafood restaurant on the Pattani Gulf that locals love for an evening out. The building is a two-storey structure at the far end of Laem Nok Village, extending right to the waterline, with both air-conditioned seating inside and open-air tables where you catch the full sea breeze. Many guests favour the deck and balcony cantilevered over the water — the view takes in fishing boats and a wide open bay. Come near sunset and it's particularly striking. A great choice for families, groups of friends, or visitors wanting seafood with a proper view.

The dish most frequently mentioned is the large garlic fried prawns — firm, bouncy, fragrant with fried garlic — and the oysters, which reviewers describe as outstandingly fresh because most ingredients come directly from local fishermen. If you want bold flavours, try the soft-shell crab with yellow curry powder or the fish-sauce fried seabass. The curry crowd has southern sour curry with fish roe, which pairs beautifully with steamed rice. There's also grilled squid, salt-baked prawns, seafood hot pot, and various stir-fries for sharing. Reviewers consistently note steady quality and a flavour level that isn't excessively spicy — children and adults eat together comfortably.

Prices are in line with a typical seafood restaurant: side dishes start around 100 THB, while crab, prawn, and shellfish are charged by weight and size. Sharing across a group is good value. Local reviewers mention variety, attentive service, clean bathrooms, good parking, and a prayer room. Opens approximately 10:00–20:00, cash only.

Worth knowing: the restaurant is at the end of a lane by the sea — follow the road through Laem Nok Village near Wat Laem Nok, past the airport, then cross the bridge. Navigation apps make it easy. During holidays or evenings the waterfront tables fill quickly — come early or call ahead to reserve: 073-330-909.
mustOrder: Soft-shell crab with yellow curry powder
blocks.bestFor: Evening seafood by the sea with family or friends, watching the sun set over Pattani Bay
blocks.spice: Adjustable — most dishes not heavily spiced

blocks.name: Rong Peep
blocks.signature: Crispy rad na, lava-egg stir-fried noodles with chicken, cheesecake, retro-style coffee
blocks.descHtml:
If you've been exploring Pattani's old town and want a place that's both filling and photogenic, Rong Peep is the spot friends recommend straight away. The name comes from the building itself — a former tin-can factory that the owners renovated into a retro Chinese-style diner with high ceilings, wooden furniture, old lanterns, and two floors packed with picture-worthy corners. Ideal for couples, a group of friends, or a family wanting a long sit in cool air conditioning.

The most talked-about menu item is rad na, both the regular crispy-noodle version and the egg-lava rad na, the latter spectacularly gooey on a plate large enough to share among two or three. Another frequent order is the lava-egg stir-fried noodles with chicken (105 THB). For dessert there's cheesecake and other sweets, and you can close the meal with a retro-style coffee or the house Rong Peep tea (55 THB per glass) — the restaurant's signature, available bottled to take home as a souvenir. Most reviews praise the food as tasty and well-priced, with the iced tea and desserts standing out. A recurring practical note: roadside parking nearby is limited, especially on holiday evenings — allow extra time.

Overall pricing sits in the middle range — roughly 101–250 THB per person — reasonable for a place where the food and the atmosphere both deliver. Open daily from 11:00 to 21:00 (kitchen closes 20:30). Some evenings feature live music, which adds to the atmosphere. Located on Ramgomutt Road Soi 2, Aneao Sub-district, right in the city centre — easy to reach from the old-town area.
blocks.bestFor: Groups or couples, café-lovers and photo-takers, lunch or dinner
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative image: café · Andy Li / Wikimedia (CC0)

blocks.name: Once Upon A Time Cafe
blocks.signature: Thai tea, seafood fried rice, homemade pies and tarts, quality drinks
blocks.descHtml:
If you're in Pattani and want a café to linger in for hours with great photos, this is the name people in town give first. Once Upon A Time Cafe is tucked behind a stationery shop on Udom Withi Road, next to Bangkok Bank in the old-town area — drive into the side alley to park easily. A husband-and-wife team built it because they wanted to give Pattani people a genuinely good café. The space is a greenhouse-style glass structure surrounded by plants, divided into air-conditioned sections, an outdoor zone, and a waterside corner, with plenty of charming spots for photos throughout. A great choice for couples or a group of friends who want to relax.

The most-ordered item is the Thai tea, which the owners describe as honest — rich, sweet, and just right. For coffee drinkers there's an espresso machine plus drip and Aeropress, using both Thai and imported beans. Popular items are the Flat White (55 THB) and the Pudpud Coffee (75 THB) — a cold brew finished with a cocoa-dusted foam cloud. On the savoury side: baked chicken rice, fried chicken waffle, beef burger, and seafood fried rice. Finish with homemade pies, tarts, cakes, and baked goods — reviewers say they're worth ordering.

Most reviews praise the atmosphere, décor, and clean bathrooms — many note it's a café best suited to those who love design and relaxation rather than hardcore coffee purists. Pricing runs 55–150 THB per person, reasonable for a café this carefully fitted out. Another plus: food and coffee are halal, making it comfortable for Muslim travellers.

Worth knowing: open daily 09:00–20:00, but on Wednesdays the kitchen closes and only drinks and bakery are served until around 18:00 — avoid Wednesday if you want a hot meal. On weekends there may be a short wait for a table, but the greenhouse atmosphere, the variety of drinks, and the menu make the wait worthwhile. It's become one of the city's most popular café stops.
blocks.bestFor: Photo café crowd, chilling all day
blocks.hours: 09:00–20:00 daily (Wed kitchen closes, drinks & bakery only until 18:00)
blocks.spice: Can be spicy if you order the Bang Bang chicken style

blocks.name: Tist Makan
blocks.signature: Fish-sauce fried sea bass, crab and wild betel leaf curry, squid stir-fried with salted egg, stir-fried liang leaves with egg
blocks.descHtml:
Tist Makan is a spacious, beautifully decorated southern Thai restaurant in central Pattani — a landmark for big meals with family or a group. The standout feature is the wide dining room: walls covered in artwork reflecting southern Thai culture, creating a warm atmosphere that photographs well from every angle. Works equally well for a relaxed lunch or an evening meal where you want to linger and talk.

The dishes most talked about and most ordered are fish-sauce fried sea bass — large, firm fish fried to a crisp aromatic skin — and crab and wild betel leaf curry, with a rich, rounded sauce that's deeply spiced in the southern style. For fried and stir-fried dishes, try squid with salted egg, just the right level of salty-rich, and stir-fried liang leaves with egg, a local vegetable that's a pleasure against steamed rice. For those who want more southern heat, there's also southern sour curry with sea bass and young coconut shoots. Reviews consistently agree: bold southern flavour, food arrives quickly, and service is good.

Pricing is reasonable for the plate sizes — the restaurant is designed for ordering multiple dishes to share, averaging a few hundred THB per person. The food is halal, so Muslim guests are comfortable. There's also a Tist Coffee zone where you can sit and have a coffee after the meal. Located on Samakkhi Road Sai B, Sabarang Sub-district, in Pattani city centre — easy to find, with parking. Open daily from late morning through to the evening.

This restaurant consistently appears on Pattani's recommended lists because it combines bold southern food, a beautiful space, and seating that comfortably handles large groups. During holidays or evenings the place fills up — for groups, call ahead to book a table, and allow a little extra time if ordering a large whole fish.
mustOrder: Crab and wild betel leaf curry
blocks.bestFor: A big meal with family or a group

blocks.text: If you want to sample several Malay-heritage spots in a single trip with someone who can explain the history as you go, look for food tours and southern Thai cooking classes through Klook and GetYourGuide. Perfect for anyone wanting to understand the Malay flavour palette at a deeper level than just ordering. Book online in advance.

blocks.title: Good to Know Before Eating in Pattani

items.title: Getting around the city
items.text: Central Pattani is compact enough to walk between old-town spots, but seafood restaurants like Laem Nok and Rusamilae are a short drive out of town. Renting a vehicle or using local taxis is recommended — Grab coverage is limited here, so allow extra waiting time.

items.title: Bring cash
items.text: Street stalls and local spots like kai kho lae, nasi dakae, and khao yam generally accept cash or PromptPay. Keep small bills handy. Cafés and larger seafood restaurants usually accept transfers.

items.title: Beat the queue
items.text: Popular spots like kai kho lae and Khao Yam Racha get crowded on weekends and holidays. Arriving before noon or in the late afternoon avoids the longest waits. Some signature items sell out by mid-afternoon.

items.title: Most restaurants here are halal
items.text: Pattani's Malay food is almost entirely halal — no pork, no alcohol. Ideal for Muslim travellers. If you're looking for pork dishes like khao man kai or roast pork rice, Chinese-run shops like Ko Chiu have them separately.

items.title: English menus are limited
items.text: Cafés and larger seafood restaurants may have picture menus or some English. Street and local stalls are usually Thai-only. Pointing to photos on your phone works well — Pattani people are warm and will always help you pick the highlights.

items.title: Tipping is optional
items.text: No obligation to tip at general restaurants. At street stalls, pay the listed price. At sit-down restaurants with table service, leaving loose change if you enjoyed it is appreciated but never expected.

blocks.title: Plan a Full-Day Pattani Food Trip
blocks.html:
Structure your Pattani food day in three sessions. Morning: start at Kai Kho Lae Yi Yoh Ramgomutt, Soi 4 Ramgomutt Road — the city's signature dish, worth doing at least once. Order both breast and leg with coconut curry sauce, 45–50 THB each. Then stop at Nasi Dakae Sabarang for coconut rice with braised tuna curry, and eat it alongside a khao yam from the stall next door. A complete meal for under 100 THB.

Midday: for seafood, head to Sun Kum Pu at Rusamilae for crab fried rice and crab noodle curry, or drive out to Kruwa Madam Laem Nok for fat garlic fried prawns with a sea view. Late afternoon, finish with Khao Yam Racha at Kama on Naklua Road (opens 3 p.m., closes 10 p.m.) — eat it with turmeric-salt grilled fish. Wrap the evening at Rong Peep or Once Upon A Time café in the old town. Southern food, seafood, and café culture — all in one day.

blocks.text: Eaten your way through the day and want to stay close to the best food? Pick a hotel in the Mueang Pattani or Rusamilae area — you'll reach every restaurant on this list easily, and wake up right in time for kai kho lae.

faq.q: Which restaurant in Pattani is the most famous — essential for a first visit?
faq.a: For a first visit, Kai Kho Lae Yi Yoh Ramgomutt on Soi 4 Ramgomutt Road is the one — the city's signature dish made by the same family for four generations, with a coconut sauce simmered for three hours and no MSG. Paired with Kama Khao Yam Racha on Naklua Road, famous for its exceptionally generous toppings, these two are the spots Pattani locals mention most often.

faq.q: What are Pattani's signature foods worth trying?
faq.a: First is kai kho lae — charcoal-grilled chicken drenched in a rich coconut curry sauce, a Malay dish unique to the Deep South border provinces. Then khao yam, a herb-packed rice salad dressed with fish sauce paired with turmeric-grilled fish. Nasi dakae — coconut-steamed rice with braised tuna curry — and seafood like crab fried rice and crab noodle curry found at restaurants along the coast.

faq.q: How much does eating in Pattani cost?
faq.a: Street and local food is very inexpensive: kai kho lae at 45–50 THB per piece, nasi dakae under 100 THB for a full meal, Khao Yam Racha at 40–100 THB per plate. Seafood restaurants like Sun Kum Pu or Kruwa Madam Laem Nok run around 100–250 THB per person, depending on how much crab and prawn you order by the kilo. Cafés like Rong Peep and Once Upon A Time are in the low hundreds.

faq.q: Do Pattani restaurants require advance booking?
faq.a: Local street spots like kai kho lae, nasi dakae, and khao man kai are walk-in only — no reservations. Queues may form on weekends. For seafood restaurants and cafés like Sun Kum Pu, Kruwa Madam Laem Nok, or Rong Peep, calling ahead for a table if you're coming as a larger group or during a long holiday weekend is a good idea.

faq.q: Are there restaurants open evening to late night in Pattani?
faq.a: Yes. Khao Yam Racha at Kama is open from 3 p.m. to 10 p.m., perfect for dinner. Seafood spots Sun Kum Pu and Kruwa Madam Laem Nok both stay open into the evening. Rong Peep café is open until around 9 p.m., a good option for an evening coffee in a vintage setting.
